description: CR-CH-076 -- Block line commands RR/DD/CC/MM in the SHARED ISPF table editor. Doubled letters on two rows form an inclusive, order-independent range; the op applies to the whole block. Single R/Rn vs block RR is preserved. BUILD ON ff-line-commands (it already parses the doubled tokens and pairs them via BlockPairValidator) with NO public-API change. The only code changes are the shared apply adapter (line_commands.rs Block arm) and a block opt-in flag on LineCommandSet (state.rs). CC/MM need an A/B target (same as single C/M); MoveBlock is gated on set.move_ so MM is disabled on Alias (move_ = false, Req 7.12). Unterminated/too-many/overlap -> non-blocking notice, marker RETAINED, no structural change, rest of the batch still applies (Req 9.4). Reusable: Alias opts in via blocks:true (Req 7.11); other hosts inherit it.
steps: RED: in crates/ff-desktop/src/shell/ispf_table_editor/state.rs mod tests, add a failing assertion that LineCommandSet::alias().blocks == true and a default set has blocks == false. Then add `pub blocks: bool` to LineCommandSet; set true in const fn alias(), false elsewhere; keep move_: false in alias() so MM stays disabled. Validates Req 9.1, 9.5.

RED: in crates/ff-desktop/src/shell/ispf_table_editor/line_commands.rs mod tests, add a blocks-enabled (and move_-enabled, for CC/MM) stub host and failing tests over Vec<StubRow>: DD/DD deletes the inclusive range; RR/RR duplicates every row in the range; CC/CC + A copies the block after the target; CC/CC + B before; MM/MM + A moves the block; reversed-order markers form the same inclusive range. Each annotated // Validates: ispf-table-editor Requirement 9.1/9.2/9.3.

RED: add failing tests for the unterminated/malformed/overlap cases: a lone DD -> non-blocking 'block not closed' notice, marker retained (act stays 'DD'), no structural change, while a well-formed I/D in the same batch still applies; three DD markers -> malformed/too-many notice, no change; overlapping DD and RR ranges -> rejected with a notice, neither applied. Add the R-vs-RR distinction test (single R repeats one row; matched RR/RR repeats the range). Validates Req 9.2, 9.4.

GREEN: implement the block path in apply_line_commands. When set.blocks, collect (backing_index, LineCommandKind) block markers instead of clearing; build a ff_line_commands::PendingCommandStore, add each marker (line = backing index, PendingReason::AwaitingPair, kind via to_block_kind), pair via BlockPairValidator::validate_pair; on Ok record the BlockPair, on Err(AwaitingPair|TooManyMarkers) push a notice and leave the Act cells uncleared (retained). Run check_overlaps across resolved pairs; on overlap push a notice and drop the overlapping pairs. Resolve CC/MM A/B from the existing targets list (reuse the single C/M target-consume logic); a CC/MM with no target is retained with the existing 'pending a target' notice. Translate each applied pair into the existing before/after/removed stable-original-index rebuild (DeleteBlock -> removed range; RepeatBlock -> clone each row in range into its own after[i]; CopyBlock+A/B -> clones to target before/after; MoveBlock+A/B -> same plus removed range). Gate MoveBlock on set.move_ (Alias move_ = false disables MM). Clear consumed block Act cells. When !set.blocks keep today's clear+notice behaviour. Keep the function/file under 400 non-test lines -- extract a block_apply.rs helper beside it (and re-export via mod.rs) if needed. NO ff-line-commands API change.

GREEN: add a full-shell egui_kittest test in crates/ff-desktop/src/shell/tests_focus.rs modelled on full_shell_alias_editor_enter_in_act_cell_applies_line_command (harness_shell(); dispatch_command_string("ALIASES"); seed three rows; request_focus(egui::Id::new(("alias_act", i))); push Event::Text for CC / CC / A on rows 0/1/2; request_focus the command line 'alias_editor_command_line'; key_press(Enter)); assert the two-row block was copied after row 2. Validates Req 9.1, 9.3.
acceptance_criteria: LineCommandSet has a blocks flag; alias() sets blocks=true and keeps move_=false.
cargo test -p ff-desktop block_ passes: DD/RR/CC(A and B)/MM apply over the stub rows; reversed markers normalise to the same inclusive range.
A lone or >2 block marker yields a non-blocking notice, retains the marker, makes no structural change, and does not abort the rest of the batch; overlapping blocks are rejected with a notice.
A single R still repeats exactly one row alongside an unrelated RR block (distinction preserved).
The full-shell CC/CC+A block-copy test passes end to end through the Alias host; MM has no effect on Alias (move_ disabled).
No change to any ff-line-commands public API; all pre-existing single-command tests still pass.
findings: DONE (branch ispf-editor-impl, worktree .worktrees/ispf-editor-impl). CR-CH-076 block line commands implemented in the SHARED adapter with NO ff-line-commands public-API change. Changes: (1) state.rs -- added `pub blocks: bool` to LineCommandSet; alias() sets blocks=true and keeps move_=false (so RR/DD/CC enabled, MM disabled per Req 7.12). (2) New sibling module block_apply.rs (~193 lines, no test mod) holds resolve_blocks<H>(rows,set,markers,targets,&mut consumed_targets,&mut result) -> BlockPlan{removed,inserts,clear}. It builds a ff_line_commands PendingCommandStore keyed by BACKING index, pairs each distinct block kind via BlockPairValidator::validate_pair (Ok -> BlockPair, Err(AwaitingPair/TooManyMarkers) -> 'block not closed' notice + markers RETAINED), runs check_overlaps (overlap -> notice + drop ALL pairs, markers retained), resolves CC/MM A/B from the shared targets list sharing consumed_targets with single C/M, and gates MoveBlock on set.move_ (MM dropped with 'not enabled' notice when move_ off). block_apply exported via mod.rs; ApplyResult::push made pub(super). (3) line_commands.rs apply_line_commands: the parse loop now routes Block markers to a `blocks` vec when set.blocks && block_enabled() (block_enabled restricts the set to EXACTLY DD/RR/CC/MM -- no II/XX/shift blocks, Req 9.1); when !set.blocks a doubled marker is cleared+ignored with a non-blocking notice (unchanged Req 4.5). After single C/M resolution it calls resolve_blocks (sharing consumed_targets) BEFORE the no-source target cleanup, then folds the BlockPlan into the SAME before/after/removed stable-original-index rebuild (clones snapshotted while indices valid; RepeatBlock clones the range into after[end]; CopyBlock/MoveBlock clone the range before/after the target; MoveBlock also marks the source range removed; plan.clear clears consumed source+target Act cells). (4) Full-shell egui_kittest test full_shell_alias_editor_cc_block_copies_after_target in tests_focus.rs drives CC/CC+A through the Alias host via a Command ===> Enter. Verification (all scoped, all GREEN, read from proxy result files): cargo check -p ff-desktop ok; cargo clippy -p ff-desktop -- -D warnings clean; cargo fmt -p ff-desktop -- --check clean; cargo test -p ff-desktop block_ = 14 passed (incl the state block_opt_in_flag_is_per_host and the full-shell block test); cargo test -p ff-desktop full_shell_alias_editor = 4 passed (no regression). No .rs over 400 non-test lines (line_commands.rs non-test ~250; block_apply.rs ~193). ASCII-only confirmed. NOTES FOR LATER STEPS: (a) For FEAT-002/003 the block path is REUSABLE -- a host opts in purely via its LineCommandSet (blocks=true, and move_=true if it wants MM); no host code change is needed to get RR/DD/CC/MM. (b) notice strings: 'block <KK> not closed (needs a matching pair)', 'overlapping block ranges rejected', 'ignored block line command "MM" (not enabled)', 'copy/move block source pending a target (A/B)'. (c) StubHost in line_commands.rs tests gained a move_enabled flag + with_move() ctor for MM coverage. (d) resolve_blocks is pub(super); block_apply is pub(crate) mod. Did NOT touch FEAT-002/003 scope. Committed locally; NOT pushed; NOT merged. Owner runs the full cargo gate before merge.
